reference_document: Kasei 11 airframe. IJN test results (試験成績) of G4M1 Model 11 aircraft No. 1 (Kasei 11, collector exhausts, no armour, Hamilton propellers) at the 9,500 kg reconnaissance-normal weight, as tabulated by WarbirdPerformanceBlog (warbirdperformance.livedoor.blog/archives/6848816.html; the original report was not read): 236.0 kt at 2,400 m and 240.0 kt at 4,200 m (true airspeed); 3,000 m in 5 min 33 s, 8,000 m in 22 min 23 s; service ceiling 9,520 m in 42 min 57 s (IJN service ceiling: 0.5 m/s climb). Power for every point is the Kasei 11 rated power, 2,350 rpm / +180 mmHg = 37.0 inHg (Navy engine manual via JA Wikipedia; TAIC Manual No. 1 p.861): the speed peaks sit just above the two rated full-throttle heights (2,200 / 4,100 m). ASSUMED, not in the source: the climbs used the same rated power; the clock started at brake release (take-off flown at take-off power, 15 deg flap, lift-off 80 / 50 ft at 86 KCAS, all estimated); climbs from the ground flew a schedule of 146 KCAS at sea level falling 0.6 kt per 1,000 ft, and the ceiling climb 112 KCAS. Both schedule speeds were FITTED to the climb times this card grades, as were the induced-drag factor (to the ceiling band and ceiling) and the zero-lift drag (to the two speeds); the climb rows therefore check the model's consistency, not an independent prediction. A ceiling climb at the model's own best-climb speed (~95 KCAS) cannot match both the ceiling band and the 8,000 m time. Not graded: the bombing-state rows (12,000 kg in parentheses, store drag unknown) and Francillon's unconditioned 120 km/h stall.
